title: CmdPal: If you update the `Command` after changing the `Title` of a fallback item, we won't hide it correctly
body:
### Provide a description of requested docs changes

Noticed in #38455 

> I think I see what it is. I think we can work around it for now, and fix the big problem later. 
> 
> If you update the `Title` of the `CommandItem` first, then the `Command`, then in `CommandItemViewModel`, we don't re-update the `Title` property when the command changes. We leave the `Title` from when the title changed (which uses the `Name` of the `Command` if the `Title` is empty)
> 
> So we can workaround this in `FallbackOpenFileItem` just by moving `Command = new NoOpCommand()` before we set the `Title`. It's dumb, but it works for 0.2

What we _should_ be doing is checking in `CommandItemViewModel` to see if when the `Command` changes if the current `_itemTitle` is empty, then also send a `UpdateProperty(Title)`

title: Shell extensions for 32-bit context menu
body:
### Description of the new feature / enhancement

PowerToys shell extensions (Image Resizer, File Locksmith, etc.) should show in both 32-bit and 64-bit context menus. Right now, they only show up in 64-bit applications like File Explorer, but it's possible to support 32-bit applications as well. A dll for each bitness would probably be the standard way of doing that.

### Scenario when this would be used?

File Explorer shows a 64-bit context menu, but some third-party software can show a 32-bit context menu with shell extensions. For example, [XYplorer](https://www.xyplorer.com/) is a popular advanced file manager. It can show a 64-bit menu but since it itself is a 32-bit application, its own context menu items can only show up in the 32-bit menu. Some people use it specifically because it can load old 32-bit shell extensions, but generally it's used as a file explorer substitute.

So, the default context menu in that app will not include the PowerToys shell extensions. By adding 32-bit versions of PowerToys' shell extensions, they will show up in the context menus for 32-bit applications.

### Supporting information

See [Attribute Changer](https://www.petges.lu/) or [TortoiseSVN](https://tortoisesvn.net/) for an example shell extension that shows in both 32 and 64-bit context menus.

### Description of the new feature / enhancement

I can enter `c:/tmp` instead of `c:\tmp` in the PowerToys Run box to open that folder in File Explorer.

But if I enter `c:/tm` and hit `Tab` autocomplete doesn't work.

That's one of possibly many scenarios where PowerToys Run _demands_ backslashes. 

It would be a good improvement to support forward slashes in all contexts where (partial) pathspecs are input.

### Scenario when this would be used?

In my default (almost only) shell, i.e. PowerShell, I can use forward slashes instead of backslashes in about any common context for pathspecs:

````text
PS❯  gi c:/tmp

        Directory: C:\


Mode                LastWriteTime         Length Name
----                -------------         ------ ----
d----        2022-03-15     16:43                  tmp

PS❯  gi c:/tm<TAB>
# TAB performs completion, result is c:\tmp\
````

This is especially convenient because, even though I'm using Windows with the _display language_ set to English, I'm French, using French computers with the French AZERTY keyboard layout, where entering a forward slash (`Shift+:`) is _way more convenient_ than entering a backslash (`AltGr+8`). title: [Run][Calculator Plugin] Infinity, -Infinity and NaN are not supported
body:
## ℹ Computer information

- PowerToys version: 0.29.3

## 📝 Provide detailed reproduction steps (if any)

Type log(-1), arcsin(2) or other functions in the launcher that would return NaN, Infinity or -Infinity.

### ✔️ Expected result

_What is the expected result of the above steps?_

Not a number (NaN)

### ❌ Actual result

_What is the actual result of the above steps?_

Nothing

---

The problem is that [`Convert.ToDecimal()`](https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/990c27718af170ca44561ca61bea424fbc80a86a/src/modules/launcher/Plugins/Microsoft.Plugin.Calculator/CalculateEngine.cs#L44) doesn't accept `NaN`, `Infinity` and `-Infinity` as input values. 

Because of that thrown exception, nothing is returned instead of [Not a number (NaN)](https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/ea21a112599da1a21ff0e5f81b7392f5903d0f61/src/modules/launcher/Plugins/Microsoft.Plugin.Calculator/Properties/Resources.resx#L127).

I already discussed this [here](https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/pull/9104#discussion_r558313813).

title: [FZ Settings] Refactor "Override Windows Snap shortcut (Win + Arrow) to move windows between zones" settings
body:
We should refactor these options:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/3206696/97712348-9b819000-1abe-11eb-802f-8d128ca06eea.png)

The first checkbox `Override Windows Snap shortcut (Win + Arrow) to move windows between zones` will have the same text but it's logical functionality changes (more explanation later).

`Move windows between zones across all monitors` remains the same.

`Move windows based on their position` is replaced by two radio buttons:
 - `Win + Left/Right to move windows based on zone index`
 - `Win + Up/Down/Left/Right to move windows based on relative position` 

The text is not final but it should give an idea that you can chose between overriding only `Win + Left/Right` and therefore `Win + Up/Down` will still work with with Windows 10 Snap, or you can choose to override all `Win + arrows` and they will move the windows in the 4 directions and completely replace Windows 10 Snap.

Right now when you check `Override Windows Snap shortcut (Win + Arrow) to move windows between zones` the behavior is `Win + Left/Right to move windows based on zone index` and if you also check `Move windows based on their position` this is `Win + Up/Down/Left/Right to move windows based on relative position`

title: bootstrapper: add cmd argument for custom log location
[File Explorer] Disabling/uninstalling thumbnail providers may require cleaning up the thumbnail cache
body:
While testing the fix for enabling/disabling the File Explorer add-ons (https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/pull/6883), i.e. preview handlers and thumbnail providers it was found that for thumbnail providers, if you enable/disable the setting may require restarting explorer **and** cleaning up the thumbnail cache. This also applies for uninstalling. 

I'm not exactly sure under what circumstances does Windows normally update the thumbnail cache, but clearing the thumbnail cache using the steps in this article: https://neosmart.net/wiki/clear-thumbnails-cache/#Method_2-4, i.e. `Disk Cleanup ->Thumbnails` can be used consistently to enable/disable the handler once the setting has been applied from PowerToys. (more context at this comment https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/pull/6883#discussion_r501415314)

We should find if this step can be avoided, or if there is a way to trigger it from code.

title: [FancyZones] Priority grid zone positions are not consistent
body:
<!--
**Important: When reporting BSODs or security issues, DO NOT attach memory dumps, logs, or traces to Github issues**.
Instead, send dumps/traces to secure@microsoft.com, referencing this GitHub issue.
-->

# Environment
```
Windows build number: 19041.172
PowerToys version: Master/0.16.0
PowerToy module for which you are reporting the bug (if applicable): FancyZones
```

# Steps to reproduce
With the _'During zone layout changes, windows assigned to a zone will match new size/position'_ setting enabled: Use the Priority Grid template layout with two zones. Add a window to the 'priority' zone (the largest zone). Add a new zone. The window will no longer be in the priority zone and will now be in the non-priority zone to the left. This occurs whenever a new zone is added to the left of the priority zone.

# Expected behavior
Windows added to the priority zone should remain in the priority zone when the number of zones are increased or decreased.

In general, when the zone count is increased or decreased windows should stay in the zone that most closely matches the position they're currently in, as is when increasing/decreasing zones they move around unintuitively.

This is because zone numbering is simply done from top-left to bottom-right without considering what position these zones are in when the zone count is higher or lower.

# Actual behavior
See the below screenshots, I am using the priority grid layout with 2 zones, I add a third zone, Visual Studio moves from the priority zone to the leftside non-priority zone. File explorer, not in the priority zone moves into the priority zone.

# Screenshots
2 zones:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/58787893/78282667-2f30b500-750c-11ea-8295-48e8d060e0c4.png)

3 zones:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/58787893/78282831-7159f680-750c-11ea-9333-042f5b1b41db.png)

# Proposed fix
The layout info for the priority grid is defined in ZoneSet.cpp, here is a code snippet for 2 and 3 zones:

```C++
        /* 2 */
        JSONHelpers::GridLayoutInfo(JSONHelpers::GridLayoutInfo::Full{
            .rows = 1,
            .columns = 2,
            .rowsPercents = { 10000 },
            .columnsPercents = { 6667, 3333 },
            .cellChildMap = { { 0, 1 } } }),
        /* 3 */
        JSONHelpers::GridLayoutInfo(JSONHelpers::GridLayoutInfo::Full{
            .rows = 1,
            .columns = 3,
            .rowsPercents = { 10000 },
            .columnsPercents = { 2500, 5000, 2500 },
            .cellChildMap = { { 0, 1, 2 } } }),
```

The `cellChildMap` for each layout should be changed such that zone positions stay consistent across zone counts. In this example the `cellChildMap` for 3 zones should be `.cellChildMap = { { 2, 0, 1 } }`. This would keep the windows in the priority zone in the priority zone, windows on the right hand side of the screen would remain on the right, and a new zone would be added on the left.

As well as this change a new overload method for `ZoneSet::AddZone` would need adding. Currently this method simply sets the zone's Id in a top-left to top-right fashion:

```C++
IFACEMETHODIMP ZoneSet::AddZone(winrt::com_ptr<IZone> zone) noexcept
{
    m_zones.emplace_back(zone);

    // Important not to set Id 0 since we store it in the HWND using SetProp.
    // SetProp(0) doesn't really work.
    zone->SetId(m_zones.size());
    return S_OK;
}
```

The new method should also take in the `cellChild` value and use that for the Id instead, something like this:

```C++
IFACEMETHODIMP ZoneSet::AddZone(winrt::com_ptr<IZone> zone, integer cellChild) noexcept
{
    m_zones.emplace_back(zone);

    zone->SetId(cellChild + 1);
    return S_OK;
}
```
